title: Purpose Clauses
subtitle: ut + subjunctive. veniō ut tē videam.
objectives: Recognize purpose clauses with ut (or nē for negative).
Understand sequence of tenses in purpose clauses.
Distinguish purpose (ut + subj.) from result (ut + subj. with signal word).

sections.heading: Purpose clauses
sections.body:
Purpose clauses express the goal or intent of an action. They use ut + subjunctive (nē for negative purpose).

veniō ut tē videam. — I come (in order) to see you.
mīlitēs mittit nē hostēs fugiant. — He sends soldiers so that the enemies may not flee.

Caesar writes: pontem fēcit ut exercitum trādūceret. — He made a bridge (in order) to lead the army across.
Cicero writes: dīcō ut discās. — I speak so that you may learn.

items.answer: He came (in order) to hear me / so that he might hear me.
I speak so that you may not be silent.

words.latin: Caesar pontem fēcit ut exercitum trādūceret.
words.gloss: Caesar made a bridge to lead the army across.
